title: Day 4 Diagnostic — Family, friends & relationships
purpose: Kiểm tra khả năng mô tả relationship bằng closeness, contact, support và evidence; đồng thời transfer sentence spine/chunks/frequency language từ Days 1–3.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best distinguishes emotional closeness from contact frequency?
options: We don't talk every day, but we're still close.
We are close because we are every day.
We talk daily, so everyone must be close.
Close means exactly how often we message.
questions.explanation: Closeness and contact frequency are different dimensions. People can remain close even when they do not communicate every day.

questions.prompt: You and a former colleague live in different cities but still message each other sometimes. Which chunk fits best?
options: We drift apart every day.
We still keep in touch.
We rely each other.
We are touching communication.
questions.explanation: 'Keep in touch' means maintaining contact over time, especially when people do not meet regularly.

questions.prompt: Why does 'I'm close to my sister, and we usually talk on weekends' work well as relationship talk?
options: It uses only difficult vocabulary.
It combines a relationship state with habitual evidence.
It proves Present Continuous is required for relationships.
It avoids saying anything about the relationship.
questions.explanation: 'I'm close to…' describes the state; 'we usually talk…' gives a recurring behavior that shows how the relationship works.

options: Every colleague is basically family to me.
He's a colleague I get along well with.
Anyone I know is my best friend.
I always rely on people I just met.
questions.explanation: 'Get along well with' accurately describes positive interaction without automatically claiming deep emotional closeness.

questions.prompt: Which sentence deliberately transfers Day 3 frequency language into today's topic?
options: We meet up every now and then.
We relationship always noun.
Every now and then means best friend.
We are friendship frequency.
questions.explanation: 'Every now and then' was learned as a frequency phrase on Day 3 and now naturally describes how often people meet.

questions.prompt: What can a listener reasonably infer from 'She was the first person I called when I had a problem'?
options: They definitely work at the same company.
The speaker likely trusts or relies on her.
They must talk every single day.
She is necessarily a family member.
questions.explanation: The behavior provides evidence of trust/support without the speaker needing to state 'I trust her' directly.

questions.prompt: In 'We don't talk EVERY day, but we keep in TOUCH,' what does the prominence help do?
options: It makes every syllable equal.
It highlights the contrast between non-daily contact and maintained connection.
It changes the sentence into past tense.
It means only one accent is correct.
questions.explanation: Contrastive prominence can guide the listener toward the intended contrast. It is a meaning choice, not a requirement to imitate one accent.

questions.prompt: Two old friends gradually become less close without one big argument. Which expression is the best fit?
options: They kept in touch strongly.
They drifted apart.
They relied on apart.
They got along into distance.
questions.explanation: 'Drift apart' describes gradual reduction in closeness, often without a single dramatic conflict.

spokenChallenge.prompt: Speak for 2 minutes about two real relationships in your life. For each, give the relationship label, closeness/contact pattern, one concrete behavior that shows the relationship, and one contrast. Reuse at least one Day 3 frequency phrase and one earlier chunk naturally.
